todo.title: To change in FM27
todo.intro: What the app advises you to change in “{{tactic}}”, most important first.
todo.introNoName: What the app advises you to change in your tactic, most important first.

todo.starterWhy: {{better}} rates {{betterFit}} in these roles against {{starterFit}}, today's form included
todo.piRemoveWhy: {{count}} instructions set for {{budget}} advised: his attributes do not back these

todo.help: This list gathers the advice from the boxes below (last matches, team instructions, player instructions, assistant's view), in the order they weigh on your results. It empties as you set your tactic in FM27 and the app reads the save again. Nothing is changed in the game: you decide.

review.title: What your last matches say
review.tooFew_one: {{count}} official match read so far: it takes 3 to judge the tactic on what it produces.
review.tooFew_other: {{count}} official matches read so far: it takes 3 to judge the tactic on what it produces.
review.scopeAll_other: Your last {{count}} official matches, all tactics together:
review.record: {{wins}} W, {{draws}} D, {{losses}} L, {{gf}} scored and {{ga}} conceded per match.
review.xg: Chances: {{xgFor}} xG created against {{xgAgainst}} conceded per match.
review.early_one: “{{tactic}}” has only {{count}} match read: too few to judge it alone, so the trend mixes several tactics.
review.early_other: “{{tactic}}” has only {{count}} matches read: too few to judge it alone, so the trend mixes several tactics.

verdict.keep: “{{tactic}}” is proving itself: you create more chances than you concede. Keep it and fix the details below rather than switching.
verdict.keepOther: “{{tactic}}”, the one you play in FM27, is proving itself on the pitch: you create more chances than you concede. Before adopting the XI suggested here, check what you would really gain: switching tactic sends the squad's understanding back down.
verdict.doubt: Over time your opponents create more chances than you with “{{tactic}}”. Start with the fixes below; if nothing changes in three matches, try the suggested XI.

finding.dominant: You are on top: {{xgFor}} xG created against {{xgAgainst}} conceded per match over {{matches}} matches. The base is sound.
finding.outplayed: You are being outplayed: {{xgFor}} xG created against {{xgAgainst}} conceded per match over {{matches}} matches.
finding.wasteful: Finishing: {{goals}} goals from {{xg}} xG. The chances are there, it is not the tactic: work on finishing in training and give it time.
finding.overperforming: Running hot: {{goals}} goals from only {{xg}} xG. It will not last at this rate: you need to create more.
finding.unluckyDefence: You concede {{goals}} goals from {{xg}} xG against: it is the keeper or bad luck more than the defensive block.
finding.sterile: Sterile possession: {{possession}}% of the ball for {{xg}} xG per match. The ball moves without hurting: speed the game up.
finding.fewChances: You create little: {{xg}} xG per match. Check the balance of the XI (creation, presence in the box).
finding.longShots: Too many long shots: {{shots}} shots per match at {{quality}} xG per shot. Better to look for the extra pass.
finding.leaky: You concede too much: {{xg}} xG per match for the opponent.
finding.bigChancesAgainst: Few shots conceded ({{shots}} per match) but big chances ({{quality}} xG per shot): balls are getting in behind your defence.
finding.pressFails: Your pressing wins little: {{value}}% of presses succeed. Your players run without winning the ball.

review.byTactic: Record of each tactic played this season
review.byTacticNote: xG difference: chances created minus chances conceded, per match (from 3 matches with figures). It is the most reliable number over few matches.
review.help: xG (expected goals) measure chances: they tell you better than the score whether a tactic works, because over five or six matches the score depends a lot on finishing luck. Friendlies do not count. The team and player instructions advised below take these matches into account.

advice.title: Your assistant's view of this eleven
advice.none: Nothing to add: everyone is in a role that suits him, and every position has cover.
advice.help: A role is only suggested when it is worth at least 0.6 point out of 20 more for the player and does not unbalance the team (width, creation, cover, presence in the box). A starter is only questioned for half a star, current form included. Cover comes first from the first team, then from a starter who can shift, then from the reserves.
advice.starter: {{pos}}: {{better}} ({{betterFit}}) would do better today than {{starter}} ({{starterFit}}) in these roles, current form included.
advice.rolesNote: Changing a role resets the player's familiarity with it: make these changes in one go, away from a big match.
advice.coverShift: {{pos}}: nobody on the bench to cover {{starter}}. If needed, {{player}} shifts from {{from}} and {{replacement}} comes in for him.
advice.coverThin: {{pos}}: nobody on the bench to cover {{starter}}.
advice.coverNone: {{pos}}: nobody at the club can cover {{starter}}. A position to recruit.

restedWhy.sharpness: {{pos}}: {{better}} ({{betterFit}}) rates higher than {{starter}} ({{starterFit}}), but he lacks match sharpness ({{value}}%). Give him late minutes or a reserve match.
restedWhy.condition: {{pos}}: {{better}} ({{betterFit}}) rates higher than {{starter}} ({{starterFit}}), but he is tired ({{value}}%). He takes his place back once rested.
restedWhy.morale: {{pos}}: {{better}} ({{betterFit}}) rates higher than {{starter}} ({{starterFit}}), but his morale is low ({{morale}}). A chat or playing time can lift him.
restedWhy.risk: {{pos}}: {{better}} ({{betterFit}}) rates higher than {{starter}} ({{starterFit}}), but the game gives him a high injury risk. He takes his place back once rested.

reason.leakyBlock: you concede {{xg}} xG per match: a mid block protects your defence better than a high press
reason.ballsBehind: few shots conceded but big chances ({{quality}} xG per shot): balls are getting in behind your high line
reason.sterile: {{possession}}% possession for {{xg}} xG per match: a higher tempo stops the opponent getting back in shape
reason.longShots: {{shots}} shots per match at {{quality}} xG per shot: too many long shots, better to look for the extra pass

tac.matchSame: Your base tactic, {{form}} {{style}}, remains the best against this opponent.
tac.matchBest: Against this opponent, play {{form}} {{style}} rather than your base tactic ({{base}}).
tac.matchHelp: Matchup inferred from the opponent's profile (formations, pressing, defence) with football rules. It starts from your base tactic: without a weakness measured in the game's report the formation stays, and a style change must gain more than the understanding it costs.
tac.matchHelpMeasured: Matchup measured on what the opponent concedes depending on the formation they face (game report), plus their profile.

why.coverStrikers: They play two strikers: two defensive midfielders (or three centre-backs) cover them.
why.thinCover: They play two strikers: with no defensive midfielder, your centre-backs are two against two.
why.winMidfield: Their midfield has two in the middle: with three centrally you win midfield.
why.widthVsScreen: Out of possession their two defensive midfielders close the middle: width pays off.
why.possessionVsLowPress: They rarely press: your short passing game will have time.
why.directVsHighPress: They press a lot: your direct game goes over the press.
why.attackLeaky: Their defence concedes often: an attacking mentality makes the most of it.
why.concedesMore: Against this formation they concede a clear-cut chance every {{every}} min ({{minutes}} min observed), more often than usual.
why.concedesLess: Against this formation they concede a clear-cut chance only every {{every}} min ({{minutes}} min observed).
why.changeForm: Changing formation costs tactical understanding (estimate: −0.3): only suggested on a weakness measured over at least 270 min.

team.label: Team
team.help: Team B: the best XI without Team A's starters, same formation and style, for rotation (cups, congested fixtures, fatigue). Team rating: A {{a}}, B {{b}}.

adjust.title: Match settings against {{name}}
adjust.intro: Same style, same shape: only what changes for this match, to be reverted after the final whistle.

marking.creator: {{target}}, {{positions}}, makes the team play: tighter marking and harder tackles for {{player}}.
marking.creatorNoSlot: {{target}} makes the team play: tighter marking for the player facing him.
marking.scorer: {{target}} is their scorer: {{player}} stays on him in the box (tighter marking).
marking.scorerNoSlot: {{target}} is their scorer: tighter marking for the defender facing him.

adjust.none: Nothing to change: your base tactic fits this opponent as it is.
adjust.help: Football rules applied to the game's team report (pressing, marking, shape out of possession, mentality, chances conceded, match threat), never more than four instructions changed: each change costs some tactical familiarity. An instruction your style already sets the same way is not repeated. Marking goes into the named player's individual instructions.

reason.highPress: they press a lot: we bypass their press
reason.lowPress: they rarely press: we build short, safely
reason.manMarking: man marking: freedom and rotations to drag them out
reason.screened: two defensive midfielders screen the centre: we go wide
reason.betweenLines: two banks of four: we play between their lines
reason.lowBlock: cautious mentality: a low block to move around
reason.twoStrikers: two strikers and no cover in our shape
reason.threat: stronger opponent: one notch more cautious

oppScreen.title: Game's Opposition screen against {{name}}
oppScreen.intro: Tactics › Opposition in FM27: one row per opposing player to set, leave the others empty.
oppScreen.footHint: Their players' foot is not read yet: it will appear at the plugin's next snapshot (paths added on 2026-11-07).
oppScreen.none: Nothing to set: the report names no key player.
oppScreen.help: Rules: tight marking "Always" on the creator, the scorer and the best-rated player; press "Always" on their keeper and centre-backs when your style presses high, otherwise only the lowest-rated of them (force the error in build-up); "Softer" tackling on the creator when he plays up front, so as not to give free kicks away; show onto the weaker foot read in the game, never for a two-footed player. The screen's dribbles and cards are not read by the plugin.

reason.creator: top assister
reason.softTackle: plays up front: no free kick given

physical.title: Fitness and rotation
physical.none: No starter needs protecting before the next match: nobody is tired, at risk of injury or playing too many matches in a row.

risk.fatigue: High injury risk according to the game (condition {{pct}}%).
risk.rhythm: High injury risk because he lacks match sharpness ({{sharpness}}%).

riskRaised.fatigue: Raised injury risk according to the game (condition {{pct}}%).
riskRaised.rhythm: Raised injury risk because he lacks match sharpness ({{sharpness}}%).

why.worn: Worn ({{pct}}%) before a match where you can rotate.
why.chained: He keeps playing: {{starts}} starts in {{days}} days ({{minutes}} minutes). That is when injuries happen.

do.swap: Play {{sub}} ({{subFit}}) instead: {{gap}} lower in these roles, a fair price.
do.swapEven: Play {{sub}} ({{subFit}}) instead: he rates just as well in these roles.
do.keep: {{sub}} ({{subFit}}) is too far behind him ({{fit}}) for this match: keep him, but take him off around the 60th minute.
do.noSub: No backup in good shape for this position: take him off around the 60th minute if the score allows.
do.rhythm: He needs to play to get his sharpness back, but not 90 minutes: plan to take him off around the 60th minute.

physical.help: The injury risk is the one FM27 shows for each player: it rises with fatigue and with a lack of match sharpness. A player counts as on a run from three starts in {{days}} days, friendlies included. The suggested backup is the best rated for the position among players who are fresh, not at risk and not on a run themselves. In the league, he is only advised if he is nearly as good as the starter; in cups or when matches come thick and fast, a wider gap is accepted. The advised XI also takes injury risk into account.

slots.label: Your FM27 tactics
slots.preview: You are looking at "{{name}}" as the plugin read it on {{date}}, with today's squad. In FM27, "{{active}}" is the active one: the rest of the app still follows it.
slots.missing: "{{name}}" has not been read yet: the plugin only reads the active tactic. Select it in FM27 (Tactics screen), advance a day or click "Refresh the game", and the app will keep it. Meanwhile you see "{{active}}".

contracts.byYear: Monthly wages freed by contract end year
contracts.soon: Contracts to deal with (18 months or less)

wages.byStatusHelp: Statuses from highest to lowest. A healthy wage bill pays higher statuses more: the average should drop with the status.
wages.overText: {{wage}} per month, more than a typical “{{status}}” ({{ref}})
wages.underText: {{wage}} per month for a “{{status}}”, less than a typical “{{other}}” ({{ref}})
wages.releaseText: {{wage}} per month saved if he leaves
wages.valueHelp: Monthly wage per level point: most expensive first.

fin.unknown: not read by the plugin yet
fin.simHelp: Contracts ending within 12 months. Enter the wage you would offer (0 = let him go): the room is recalculated. Nothing is saved.
fin.effect: Effect on the wage bill: {{delta}} per month
fin.afterUnknown: the room will show once the board budget is known
fin.noBoard: No board objectives in this snapshot yet. The plugin reads them at every capture (club section of chemins.json): advance a day in FM27.
fin.billGame: per month, from the game (whole squad: {{squad}}, loanees included)

loans.none: No loaned-out players. They are read with the transfer targets (LireCibles setting, "pretes" source in chemins.json) when the game date changes.
loans.help: A young player who doesn't play on loan barely progresses: recall him or find another club next window.

dressing.unknown: not read by the plugin yet
dressing.noMorale: Player morale is not read by the plugin yet. Once it is, you will see who is unhappy and how it affects buy-in to your tactics.
dressing.leadersHelp: Sorted by Leadership then Determination. A leader with low morale weighs on the whole group.

cmp.help: Highlighted: best in the row. The reference role's key attributes are in bold. The list also includes the game's targets when the plugin provides them.

prog.title: Level since {{date}}
prog.snapsRange_one: 1 snapshot, on {{from}}. Import one at each new game date to see the curves.
prog.howTo: Level is the average of their attributes: it moves little. Attribute points tell better what they gained or lost (+3 = three attributes each up one point, for instance). Green curve: improving; red: declining; grey: stable.
prog.pointsHelp: Attribute points gained or lost since their first snapshot (sum of each attribute's change).
prog.recentHelp: Attribute points gained or lost over the last 90 game days.

depth.help: Level today → {{s1}} → {{s2}}. The game hides potential: the projection follows the average age curve (strong up to 22, decline after 30), then the real trend once snapshots are several months apart.
depth.fromTactic: Same style, formation and XI as Tactics > Line-up: change them there and this view follows.
depth.fromGame: XI read from your FM27 tactic (or FM Immersion's if you pick it in Tactics > Line-up).

cal.help: Two matches 3 days apart or less: rotate the most tired players.
cal.none: The fixture list comes with the latest plugin version. Meanwhile, rotation is based on current condition and sharpness.
cal.rustyHelp: Give them minutes in cup games or late in matches to regain sharpness.

roles.help: Each cell shows the fit for the best {{phase}} role at that position. Pills: natural positions. Grey numbers: out of position (the game adds a familiarity penalty). Dashed circle: out of position but better than at his own, worth a try. Hover a cell to see the role.

how.keys: 70%: the role's key attributes, weighted by importance.
how.base: 20%: the position's basic attributes (for a centre-back: marking, tackling, heading, positioning…).
how.engine: 10%: "match engine" attributes (acceleration, pace, anticipation, decisions), useful everywhere outfield.
how.foot: Stronger foot: on a flank, −0.5 if the foot does not match (−1 if one-footed). Inverted roles want the foot opposite to the flank.
how.staff: Your staff's opinion: for your own players, the rating goes up or down with their current-ability stars compared with the first-team average (one star of difference = 1.5 points, 2.5 points at most). Players from other clubs are still rated on attributes alone.

style.whichHelp: Each style's requirements compared with the profile of the 16 best available outfield players. Pick a style for details.
style.profileHelp: Average out of 20. Highlighted: what the selected style needs.
style.rolesHelp: Fit = weighted average of the role's key attributes. Injured players excluded.
style.effHelp: New in FM27: a gauge tells whether the team will carry out your instructions. FM Immersion estimates it here; the game's real gauges are under "Effectiveness" once the plugin reads them.
style.simplify: Simplify instructions or plan training time.
style.allClose: All styles are within {{gap}} of each other: your squad doesn't favour any. Pick your project's style; FM Immersion builds the best eleven for each.

why.large: More width to move the ball around and stretch the opponent. The game only offers this at the start of a season; the effect is a small bonus.
why.short: Less ground to cover when pressing and winning the ball back. The game only offers this at the start of a season; the effect is a small bonus.
why.long: Space behind the opponent for quick attacks. The game only offers this at the start of a season; the effect is a small bonus.
why.narrow: A tight game for second balls and early crosses. The game only offers this at the start of a season; the effect is a small bonus.
why.min: As little space as possible for the opponent against a low block. The game only offers this at the start of a season; the effect is a small bonus.
why.normal: No clear preference for this style: keep normal dimensions.

eff.none: The game's effectiveness gauges are not in this snapshot yet. Meanwhile, FM Immersion's estimate is under "Playing style".
eff.snapsSub: import every week to track progress

proj.help: FM Immersion measures the gap between your squad and this style, then derives the positions to sign and each player's work. Natural formations for this style: {{forms}}.
proj.developSub: 23 or younger, close to the level

verdict.step: Gradual switch possible: keep {{rec}} and add instructions from your project.
verdict.no: Not yet: stay with {{rec}} for now.

c.readyHelp: positions at target level (7 of 11 advised)
c.abilityHelp: reading of the game vs. style complexity

proj.eta: With the same squad, a safe switch around {{date}}.
proj.etaNever: With the same squad, the switch does not happen within 3 years: you need to sign players.
proj.tipRecruit_one: Signing speeds everything up: {{count}} more ready position needed to reach 7 of 11.
proj.tipRecruit_other: Signing speeds everything up: {{count}} more ready positions needed to reach 7 of 11.
proj.tipBridge: Bridge style: {{bridge}} is almost as suitable as {{rec}} and closer to your project.
proj.tipGauge: In match, check the game's tactical effectiveness gauge before switching: it has the final say.
proj.switchHelp: Projection: each player progresses along the age curve (or his real trend), attributes shifted accordingly. Ignores departures and signings.
proj.noRecruit: No position to sign at this target level.
proj.recruitAll: For all signings, the style needs: {{list}}.
proj.collectiveMore: Also: team cohesion for buy-in, match preparation for the opposition report.
proj.trainingHelp: Target role: his position's role for a starter in the target XI, otherwise the project role he fits best. Areas: his 3 weakest key attributes for that role, for individual training.
proj.trainingDetail: The player-by-player detail (target role, attributes to work on, intensity) is in the next step, Training.
proj.fromTactic: Your game plan is your tactic: {{style}} in {{form}} ({{source}}). Mercato, training, scouting and player pages all build on it.

targets.title: Transfer targets · {{style}} {{form}}
targets.help: Players from your shortlist, your recruitment targets and those on trial, read from the game and kept in FM Immersion. For each one, FM Immersion tells what they would add to your target XI ("Recruitment and training"): starter if better than the current starter, backup if better than your current backup in that position, otherwise nothing. Click a name to compare.
targets.none: No targets yet. This needs FM27 plugin 0.4.0 with the LireCibles setting on: it reads your shortlist and recruitment targets on each new game day. Meanwhile, the profiles to look for are under "Recruitment and training".
targets.noneRead: The plugin read the game's lists but found no player ({{status}}). Add players to your shortlist, or check targetSources in the snapshot.
targets.gainHelp: {{gain}} pt out of 20 against the current starter

pi.title: Player instructions
pi.help: Picked from the player's attributes against their own level, position, foot, roles and the style. An instruction the game locks for the role is never suggested.
pi.locks: Locks inferred from the roles (screening, covering, dropping, outlet: pressing locked to “Less often”; pressing roles: “More often”). If you spot another padlock in game, say so and the rule will be extended.
pi.nothing: Nothing to add: the role is enough.
pi.switch: Role {{phase}}: switch from {{from}} to {{to}} to allow “{{what}}”.

why.gkShort: good with his feet, suits short distribution

It is the week that grows attributes most (33.3 CA over a season against 10.7 with no training); tactical sessions do no better than rest for attributes, they only feed tactical effectiveness.

yield.title: What each session yields
yield.intro: CA gained over a 100-match season by an 18-year-old with only this session each week (harvestgreen22's measurement). No training: 10.7. Best measured week, four different sessions: {{best}}.
yield.help: A tactical session grows attributes no more than rest: it feeds tactical effectiveness (42.7% wins against 39.2% with eight sessions a week, at the cost of injuries). The same session three times yields less than four different sessions. The attacking and defensive variants count as the measured (balanced) ones.

train.metaHelp: AlexJeuVideal's method ("ENTRAINEMENT FM 27 META EFFICACITÉ 1.1" pack): one block Pressing Trap, Line of Engagement, Build-Up; one block Pressing Trap, Chance Creation, In-Possession Shape; the day before the match Ball Progression, Defensive Block, Conditioning. Everything else is rest. Load the .fmf file shown in the Training screen.

train.rule1: Day after a match: full rest. Day before: a single preparation session. Another full rest day whenever there is room.
train.rule2: Group development sessions on one or two days: same development, far fewer injuries. Four different sessions are enough.
train.rule3: The number of tactical sessions follows your tactical effectiveness: many while it is low, few once the tactic is understood. Don't change tactic along the way.
train.rule4: A youngster develops mostly by playing: if he doesn't play, training won't save him. Loan or minutes.
train.rule5: Judge over at least two months with "What it really gives", not over one week: luck is strong.
train.source: "Freedom" method (FM Scout, FM27 training schedules): 44 schedules, 4-week themed cycles. The article ships no .fmf files: FM Immersion rebuilds each day with FM27's sessions, steered by your target style. Copy it into the game's Training screen. Adjusted from AlexJeuVideal's benchmark ("The truth about tactical effectiveness"): Rest the day after every match, 2 pressing trap sessions a week, priority to build-up, chance creation, line of engagement and out-of-possession shape, full rest in three-match weeks.

learn.howIntro: The numbers on screen don't tell the whole story. According to community tests on FM27, the game makes two calculations, roughly each month and for each player.
learn.step1: His age, the room below his potential, his match minutes and the level of opposition, his professionalism, training facilities, injuries, and some luck. Training only plays a small part.
learn.step2: This is where training acts: each session's share of the week, the individual focus, the trained role and the coach of the group decide which attributes rise.
learn.factorsTitle: What matters, from most to least
learn.factor1: Age: 16-18 is the golden age; it stays strong up to 21, then slows; almost nothing after 24 (27 for goalkeepers). After 30, the physical side declines.
learn.factor2: Room below potential: the closer a player gets to his potential, the slower he grows.
learn.factor3: Minutes: after 18, this is factor number one, and minutes against good opponents count more. A youngster who doesn't play doesn't develop, whatever the training.
learn.factor4: Professionalism (hidden): by far the personality trait that matters most, ahead of ambition and determination. Mentoring can raise it in a youngster.
learn.factor5: Training facilities: they affect the whole squad. Youth facilities only affect the quality of new talents.
learn.factor6: Coaches: each coaching group steers its attributes. The Fitness group covers nearly half of what matters: put your best coach there, and keep every coach's workload reasonable.
learn.factor7: Intensity: double for fit players brings a little more development, at the cost of a few more injuries.
learn.howHelp: No official formula is published: these are benchmarks from tests repeated over whole seasons, with a lot of month-to-month luck. Judge over at least two months, with "What it really gives" in This week.
learn.squadIntro: What each player can still gain, from his age, his room below potential (if CA/PA is read), his playing time and injuries. Each player's detail is in Individual.
learn.minutes: {{list}}: youngsters with room to grow who rarely play. Their playing time holds them back: start them, bring them on, or loan them to a club where they'll play.

learn.squadHelp: Playing time is compared with the most used player in the squad. Without CA/PA reading (plugin option), room below potential is not counted.
learn.teIntro: In FM27, the first team mainly trains for the next match. The most complete test (same club, three seasons per setup, 47 players) shows the trade-off:
learn.teLesson1: Never leave training to your assistant: 14 fewer points, three times more injuries, and youngsters developing the wrong attributes.
learn.teLesson2: Tactical sessions win matches (about +4% wins with 8 a month) but cost injuries: 24 a month add almost nothing and nearly double the days injured.
learn.teLesson3: Tactical sessions don't raise attributes: conditioning and ball work do.
learn.teLesson4: Changing tactic resets understanding: training only pays if the tactic stays the same.
learn.teHelp: jamiebolden's FM27 test (Bradford, Premier League 2032/33, each setup played three times from the same save). Win rate / effectiveness curve by harvestgreen22 and the playgm forum, quoted by ZaZ on FM-Arena ("Training Schedules", November 2026), who advises no more tactical sessions beyond 50%. Effectiveness breakdown: research by Chinese players quoted by ZaZ, to take as rough guides.
learn.indiv1: Up to 23, Quickness for a slow player: pace and acceleration matter most in matches, and they stop improving after that.
learn.indiv2: A starter trains the role of your tactic: he knows it better, and that counts in your tactical effectiveness.
learn.indiv3: A youngster outside the XI can train only an out-of-possession role (Defensive Midfielder for defenders, Attacking Midfielder for the others): that setting gave the most growth in tests.
learn.indiv4: A focus that gives nothing in three months: change it. The focus doesn't create growth, it steers it.
learn.indiv5: From 28, the focus no longer makes a player grow: a mental attribute of the role can still rise, the rest is maintained.
learn.sources: Tests by harvestgreen22 (FM-Arena, 50 schedules, one 100-match season each), jamiebolden (fm-scoring, tactical effectiveness on FM27, with a test on the game's training code) and AlexJeuVideal (tactical effectiveness), plus FM Dossier and Passion4FM guides on personality and playing time. Sports Interactive publishes no formula.
learn.teLesson5: Effectiveness pays most early on: from 0 to 20%, +15% wins; from 40 to 50%, +3%; from 50 to 100%, barely +1.6%. Beyond 50%, keep two sessions a week and let development take over.
learn.teLesson6: Tactical effectiveness is half understanding (players' tactical ability, simple instructions, training, matches played), a quarter player buy-in, and the opposition report. A player's tactical ability follows Anticipation, Decisions, Composure, Concentration and Versatility. Every match played raises it, every day without a match lowers it a little.

scout.help: The figures come from the game's real values (CA, PA, age, value, wage, contract), not from scout opinions. Growth: CA rises every season, fast before 21 then less and less, never above PA, and less if he doesn't play for you (backup: 70%, to loan out: 60%). Sale: the value of a player of that level and age on the market read, a bit more for a youngster on a long contract. Buy: his value, more with a long contract, less near the end of it, free if he has no club. Profit: sale − buy − wages. These are FM Immersion estimates to know where to look: real negotiations and growth are the game's.

home.title: Home
home.heading: Welcome to FM Immersion
home.intro: Create your FM27 career: FM Immersion follows it through the plugin, and every mode uses it. Photorealistic faces install even without a career.
home.lead: A dashboard for your FM27 career: it reads your game without writing anything to it and helps you decide.

editorial.title: The column
editorial.tone_crisis_0: {{count}} matches without a win, and the silence after games says it all. This is no longer a rough patch, it is a trend, and hoping will not reverse it: a reaction is needed, fast.
editorial.tone_crisis_1: You can talk about bad luck once, twice. Not {{count}} times. {{club}} must look in the mirror: the method is not working, and every week that passes makes the recovery more expensive.
editorial.tone_crisis_2: The spiral has begun. In moments like these, a dressing room looks for a culprit or a leader. At {{club}}, we are still waiting to see which one stands up.
editorial.tone_hot_0: {{count}} matches unbeaten: {{club}} are no longer playing to survive, they are playing to win, and it shows. The hardest part remains: keeping it going.
editorial.tone_hot_1: Some runs are luck, others tell the story of a team. {{club}}'s ({{count}} matches) belongs to the second kind: the plan is clear, the players believe.
editorial.tone_hot_2: Let us not spoil the moment: {{count}} matches without defeat, and a team that now knows how to suffer together. That is often where memorable seasons are born.
editorial.tone_win_0: One win does not make a season, but this one matters: {{club}} did what was needed, when it was needed. To be confirmed next match.
editorial.tone_win_1: The attitude mattered more than the score: {{club}} played to win. That is the only way to build something.
editorial.tone_win_2: Three points that lift the mood and the table. {{club}} did not get everything right, but they were there when it counted.
editorial.tone_draw_0: A point is better than nothing, but {{club}} looked like a team playing not to lose. At this rate the table will not move.
editorial.tone_draw_1: A draw and mixed feelings: we saw things, we did not see the end. {{club}} must learn to kill games.
editorial.tone_draw_2: A draw that suits nobody. {{club}} held on, {{club}} built, but lacked that little extra that makes a great week.
editorial.tone_loss_0: Defeats happen. What matters is what {{club}} make of it: a lesson, or the start of a bad habit. Answer next week.
editorial.tone_loss_1: No drama, but no excuses either: {{club}} lost to {{opponent}} because they were worse, full stop. The good news is that this can be fixed.
editorial.tone_loss_2: Losing is part of the game; losing without reacting is not. {{club}} will be judged on their response.
editorial.tone_quiet_0: A quiet week, and sometimes that is the best news: time to work, heal, prepare. Judgement comes on the pitch.
editorial.tone_quiet_1: No match, no noise. Weeks like these are for fixing what there is no time to fix otherwise.
editorial.tone_quiet_2: The calm before what comes next. At {{club}}, they are sharpening the routines.

editorial.fans_hot_0: The stands sing until the final whistle: the supporters believe.

editorial.fans_hot_2: The supporters have found their team again, and it shows.
editorial.fans_win_0: The stands leave with a smile.
editorial.fans_win_1: Warm applause at the final whistle: the supporters approved.
editorial.fans_win_2: In the terraces, they savour it without getting carried away.
editorial.fans_draw_0: The stands were left wanting more.
editorial.fans_draw_2: The supporters expected better, and do not hide it.

editorial.tone_cupOut_0: A cup exit always leaves a bitter taste. {{club}} had a chance to write a fine story against {{opponent}}; it closed too soon.
editorial.tone_cupOut_1: Going out of the cup means losing a possible night to remember. {{club}} must turn the page quickly and focus on the league.
editorial.tone_cupOut_2: The cup is unforgiving: one bad night and it is over. {{club}} pay dearly for their evening against {{opponent}}.
editorial.fans_cupOut_0: In the stands, disappointment runs deep: many hoped for a long run.
editorial.fans_cupOut_1: The fans left with heads down, the cup was their little escape this season.

editorial.board_cupOut_0: The board notes the exit and expects a reaction in the league.
editorial.board_cupOut_1: At the club, people point out that the cup also brought in revenue: the exit is costly.
editorial.board_cupOut_2: The board is not panicking, but the message is clear: no more slip-ups in the league.

a.feel_sacked_0: It is a blow, I will not hide it. The board made its choice; I respect it, even if I do not share it.
a.feel_sacked_1: In this job you know it can happen. But when it does, it hurts. I still had so much to build here.
a.feel_sacked_2: I found out in the chairman’s office, in a few minutes. Football moves fast, sometimes too fast.
a.feel_left_0: With a lot of emotion. You do not leave {{club}} like any other club.
a.feel_left_1: It was a considered decision, not a whim. But on my last day at the training ground, I had a lump in my throat.
a.feel_left_2: Calmly. I leave with my head held high and the feeling of a job well done.
a.memory_trophy_0: The title in {{season}} ({{trophy}}). Seeing that dressing room lift the trophy is why we do this job.
a.memory_trophy_1: {{trophy}} in {{season}}, of course. Nobody expected us there, and we did it together.
a.memory_win_0: The {{score}} against {{opponent}}. That day, everything we worked on during the week came off.
a.memory_win_1: The {{score}} win over {{opponent}}. The ground was still singing an hour after the final whistle.
a.memory_none_0: The people. The players, the staff, the club employees. They are what {{club}} is.
a.memory_none_1: The mornings at the training ground before anyone else arrived. I will not forget that calm.
a.player_0: {{name}}. {{count}} goals with me, always at training before everyone else. A big future ahead.
a.player_1: I think of {{name}}: {{count}} goals and a perfect attitude. The kind of player every manager dreams of.
a.player_none_0: I do not want to single anyone out: it is the whole squad that stood out.
a.why_sacked_good_0: Honestly, I do not know. The results were there, {{wins}} wins in {{played}} matches. You will have to ask the board.
a.why_sacked_good_1: The numbers speak for me. But in football you are not always judged on numbers.
a.why_sacked_bad_0: The results did not come, {{losses}} defeats, I own that. We lacked consistency and I am the first one responsible.
a.why_sacked_bad_1: We dropped too many silly points. The squad had the quality; I did not find the right balance in time.
a.why_left_next_0: The {{next}} project convinced me. It is a new challenge and I could not let it pass.
a.why_left_next_1: When {{next}} called, I felt it was the moment. The cycle here had run its course.
a.why_left_none_0: I felt I had given everything. It was time to make way for someone with fresh energy.
a.why_left_none_1: I will take a step back, watch matches, learn. Then I will go again.
a.fans_0: Thank you. For every away trip, every song, every rainy night. I will always support {{club}}.
a.fans_1: Keep pushing behind the team. The club is bigger than any manager.
a.fans_2: Simply thank you. You made me feel at home from day one.

streak_winless.tv: {{count}} games without a win. Is doubt creeping into the dressing room?
streak_winless.radio: {{count}} games without winning. What's not working?

streak_unbeaten.tv: {{count}} games unbeaten. Has this team become impossible to beat?

youthDebut.local: {{name}}, {{age}}, played his first game with the first team. Has the club found a gem?
youthDebut.tv: At {{age}}, {{name}} is getting his first taste of top football. Did you hesitate to throw him in?

bigWin.tv: {{score}} against {{opponent}}, your biggest win of the season. A message to the others?
bigWin.local: {{score}}: the stands were rocking against {{opponent}}. Your team's best game this season?

runEnded.local: After {{count}} games without a win, you finally win. Is it a relief?
runEnded.radio: That's the {{count}}-game winless run over! Did you celebrate in the dressing room?

pressure.tabloid: Your job is said to be at risk ({{status}}). Are you afraid of being sacked?
pressure.tv: The board has doubts, we hear ({{status}}). Do you still have their backing?

fans.local: The fans are unhappy ({{status}}). Do you have a message for them?
fans.tabloid: There are boos in the stands ({{status}}). Can you hear the fans' anger?

exClub.tabloid: You're up against {{opponent}}, your old club. Revenge on your mind?
exClub.tv: Facing {{opponent}} takes you back. What memories do you keep of that club?

contract.local: {{name}}'s contract ends in {{months}} months. Will he sign a new deal?
contract.tabloid: {{name}} is said to be ready to leave for free in {{months}} months. Are you losing him?

unhappy.tabloid: Word is {{name}} is sulking and doesn't feel wanted. Is there a problem in the dressing room?
unhappy.radio: {{name}} doesn't look happy right now. Have you spoken to him?

signing.local: {{name}} has just joined the club. What role will he have in your team?
signing.tv: The arrival of {{name}} has got people talking. Is he the missing piece?

exit.tabloid: {{name}} has gone. Rumour has it you pushed him out?
exit.local: {{name}} leaving leaves a gap. How will you replace him?

longInjury.local: {{name}} is out for several weeks. Is that a big blow?
longInjury.radio: Without {{name}} for a while, who steps in?

linked.tabloid: You're being linked with {{other}}. Can you confirm talks?
linked.tv: Your name is doing the rounds at {{other}}. Can you guarantee you'll still be here next season?

followUp_broken.tabloid: Before {{pastOpponent}}, you said: “{{quote}}” After this defeat, do you stand by that?
followUp_broken.radio: You told us: “{{quote}}” Tonight those words sound a bit hollow, don't they?

followUp_kept.tabloid: After {{pastOpponent}}, you said: “{{quote}}” Tonight the reaction came. Was that a message to the players?
followUp_kept.radio: “{{quote}}”, you said after {{pastOpponent}}. Message received, it seems?

followUp_denied.tabloid: Not long ago you said: “{{quote}}” And yet your name keeps coming up. Were you lying to us?
followUp_denied.radio: You denied it: “{{quote}}” But the rumour is back. Same answer?

followUp_again.tabloid: Last time, against {{pastOpponent}}, you said: “{{quote}}” Time to prove it?
followUp_again.radio: “{{quote}}”: that was your line after {{pastOpponent}}. Does it still hold for this game?

echo.other: On this subject, you already told us: "{{echo}}" {{question}}
echo.tabloid: Last time you gave us: "{{echo}}" Should we still believe it? {{question}}

echoMany.other: "{{echo}}": that's what you've been saying for {{times}} press conferences. {{question}}
echoMany.tabloid: "{{echo}}", you've been repeating it for {{times}} press conferences. Got anything else to say? {{question}}

stakes_cup.ambitious: We want to go all the way in this cup. We'll pick a team to win.
stakes_cup.humble: Every round is a trap. We respect this opponent and we'll play our game.
stakes_cup.humour: You win a cup by winning every round. I haven't found another way yet.
stakes_cup.ambitious_2: We won't sacrifice this game. A cup is a chance to make club history.
stakes_cup.ambitious_3: My team will be competitive. I want to get through this round.
stakes_cup.humble_2: There are no small opponents in a cup. We'll take it very seriously.
stakes_cup.humble_3: They'll play the game of their lives. We have to match that.
stakes_cup.humour_2: I was asked if I'd rotate. Mostly I'll rotate the ball.
stakes_cup.humour_3: A cup comes down to one game. I'd rather it was ours.

stakes_europe.ambitious: We wait all year for nights like these. We're going there to win, not to make up the numbers.
stakes_europe.humble: We're discovering this level. We'll learn, and we'll fight.
stakes_europe.humour: I told the players: in Europe the ball is the same. It just moves faster.
stakes_europe.ambitious_2: We worked hard to live nights like this. We won't settle for taking part.
stakes_europe.ambitious_3: I want Europe to discover this team.
stakes_europe.humble_2: It's another level, we know that. We'll learn fast and give everything.
stakes_europe.humble_3: We don't have the experience of these games. We have the hunger, and that's a lot already.
stakes_europe.humour_2: I've checked everyone's passport. The rest we'll see on the pitch.
stakes_europe.humour_3: The stadiums are bigger in Europe. The goals are still the same size.

stakes_top.ambitious: We're not afraid of anyone. If we play our football, we can win this.
stakes_top.humble: They have a very good team. We'll have to be perfect.
stakes_top.humour: If we win, it was a big game. If we lose, the season goes on. I prefer the first option.
stakes_top.ambitious_2: This is the kind of game that shows what a team is made of. We're going to go for the win.
stakes_top.ambitious_3: They're ahead, so it's up to us to go and get them. We won't go there to defend.
stakes_top.humble_2: They're ahead in the table for a reason. We'll need a very big performance.
stakes_top.humble_3: We're not favourites, and that suits us fine. We'll play without pressure.
stakes_top.humour_2: I told the players it was a game like any other. Nobody believed me.
stakes_top.humour_3: If we win, you can write that it's a turning point. If we lose, we'll talk again next week.

stakes_rival.ambitious: Winning this would give us breathing space. We're ready.
stakes_rival.humble: Three points like any other, even if we know what they mean.
stakes_rival.humour: Six points, three points… I'll leave the maths to you. I just want to win.
stakes_rival.ambitious_2: We've had this game circled for a long time. We want to pull ahead.
stakes_rival.ambitious_3: If we win, we give ourselves real breathing room. We'll go all out.
stakes_rival.humble_2: They're chasing the same goals as us. It'll be tight to the end.
stakes_rival.humble_3: They have as much to lose as we do. The first one to make a mistake will pay.
stakes_rival.humour_2: I leave the maths to my assistant. All I know is three points beats one.
stakes_rival.humour_3: I'm told it's a six-pointer. I hope they really give us all six.

theirScorer.confident: We have a plan. He won't see much of the ball.
theirScorer.calm: He's a very good player, we'll be careful as a team.
theirScorer.deflect: I don't talk about the other team's players. I talk about mine.
theirScorer.confident_2: We've studied him closely. We know how to cut off his supply.
theirScorer.confident_3: My defenders know what to do. He's in for a difficult evening.
theirScorer.calm_2: One player doesn't make a team. We'll watch the space, not just him.
theirScorer.calm_3: He's a quality player, no doubt. We'll respect him without obsessing over him.
theirScorer.deflect_2: I'd rather talk about my strikers. They know how to score too.
theirScorer.deflect_3: My players are what interests me. The rest we sort out in training.

injuries.confident: The squad is deep enough. Whoever plays is ready.
injuries.calm: We deal with it. That's football, it happens to everyone.
injuries.firm: I'm not looking for excuses. Eleven players will be on the pitch.
injuries.confident_2: The players who've had less time are waiting for this moment. They'll take their chance.
injuries.confident_3: We've prepared for this. Whoever starts will be ready.
injuries.calm_2: We make do with what we have. The medical staff are doing a huge job.
injuries.calm_3: It happens in a season. We'll adapt, as always.
injuries.firm_2: I won't talk about the injured. I'll talk about the ones who are here.
injuries.firm_3: No excuses. We have a squad and it has to deliver.

form.confident: The results show we're on the right track.
form.calm: We look at the next game, not the last ones.
form.firm: It's not good enough. We have to do better, and we know it.
form.confident_2: The team is growing. The results are following the work we put in.
form.confident_3: We've found a balance. I'm confident about what comes next.
form.calm_2: Runs, good or bad, never last. We stay focused on the next game.
form.calm_3: I'm not getting carried away. There's good and less good.
form.firm_2: We lack consistency. I want the same level every week.
form.firm_3: We can do much better, and I'm going to demand it.

ourScorer.confident: He's full of confidence, and the team finds him really well.
ourScorer.calm: He scores, great, but the whole group works for it.
ourScorer.firm: Nobody is bigger than the team. Goals will come from everywhere.
ourScorer.confident_2: He's in incredible form. We'll keep playing for him.
ourScorer.confident_3: He's full of confidence, and when he's like that he's very hard to stop.
ourScorer.calm_2: He scores, but look at all the work behind it. It's collective.
ourScorer.calm_3: I'm happy for him, but I don't want us to depend on one player.
ourScorer.firm_2: If one day he doesn't score, others will have to. I don't want dependence.
ourScorer.firm_3: Nobody is indispensable here. He knows that better than anyone.

congestion.confident: We have a squad for this. Everyone will get a chance.
congestion.calm: We manage the minutes day by day with the medical staff.
congestion.firm: Fatigue is no excuse. Whoever plays will have to give everything.
congestion.confident_2: I trust my whole squad. Those who play less will be ready.
congestion.confident_3: This is the moment to see the depth of our group.
congestion.calm_2: We look at the physical data every day. We'll make the right calls.
congestion.calm_3: We'll have to manage it and rotate a bit. That's the schedule, we deal with it.
congestion.firm_2: I don't want to hear about tiredness. Whoever is picked gives everything.
congestion.firm_3: We're professionals. Playing often is the job.

titleRace.ambitious: Yes, we think about it. We'd be mad not to.
titleRace.humble: There are too many games left. We'll talk about the title if it comes.
titleRace.humour: The champagne is on ice. Lots of ice. At the back of the fridge.

result_W.praise: The players were outstanding tonight. This win belongs to them.
result_W.calm: A good win, but there are still things to fix.
result_W.ambitious: That's what I expect every week. And we can do even better.
result_W.praise_2: We were patient, waited for the right moment and the players struck. I'm proud of them.
result_W.praise_3: Everyone defended, everyone attacked. This is a win for the whole group.
result_W.calm_2: The score flatters us at times. We suffered in spells and we'll need to fix that.
result_W.calm_3: Three points is what matters. We'll go over the rest on video.
result_W.ambitious_2: We showed what we're worth. Now we have to do it again every weekend.
result_W.ambitious_3: I want this team to scare people. Tonight we took a step in that direction.

result_D.confident: We had the chances, the win will come next time.
result_D.calm: A point, we'll take it. We move on.
result_D.firm: It's not enough. We should have won this game.
result_D.confident_2: We controlled the game for long spells. Keep this intensity and the wins will come.
result_D.confident_3: I see a team that's improving. The result doesn't tell the whole story.
result_D.calm_2: A draw isn't a disaster. We take the point and get back to work.
result_D.calm_3: It was an even game and an even result. I won't make a drama out of it.
result_D.firm_2: With the chances we had, we have to win. We need to be more clinical.
result_D.firm_3: I'm frustrated. We let two points slip and we won't get them back.

result_L.protect: I won't let anyone pile on my players. We lose together.
result_L.selfCritical: I made the wrong calls tonight. That's on me.
result_L.firm: That's unacceptable. I'll be having a word with the group.
result_L.protect_2: My players kept trying to the end. The criticism is for me, not for them.
result_L.protect_3: We lost a game, not our season. The group will stick together.
result_L.selfCritical_2: The game plan didn't work, and I chose it. I have to prepare these games better.
result_L.selfCritical_3: I was too slow to make changes. I take full responsibility.
result_L.firm_2: What we showed tonight isn't worthy of this shirt. That will change.
result_L.firm_3: Some players weren't at the level. They know it, and they'll hear it from me.

cup_W.ambitious: We have no limits. We play every round to win it.
cup_W.humble: We take it one round at a time, no getting carried away.
cup_W.humour: I'll watch the draw tomorrow. Tonight, we enjoy it.
cup_W.ambitious_2: I want to go as far as possible. Why not all the way?
cup_W.ambitious_3: Every round we get through gives us confidence. We want to keep dreaming.
cup_W.humble_2: There are plenty of teams stronger than us left. We enjoy it without getting carried away.
cup_W.humble_3: We'll enjoy tonight. Tomorrow we think about the league again.
cup_W.humour_2: I won't watch the draw. My players will, and they'll tell me.
cup_W.humour_3: The fans are already asking me about the final. I told them to book the coach, just in case.

cup_D.ambitious: We have what it takes to finish the job.
cup_D.humour: We'll have to come back. Good thing we like this ground.

cup_L.protect: The players gave everything. We'll bounce back together.
cup_L.selfCritical: We weren't at the level, and I take my share of the blame.
cup_L.firm: A knockout like that must never happen again.
cup_L.protect_2: The players deserved better. We'll move forward together.
cup_L.protect_3: I don't just remember the exit. I remember the commitment.
cup_L.selfCritical_2: I made choices for this game. They weren't the right ones.
cup_L.selfCritical_3: We couldn't raise our level. That starts with me.
cup_L.firm_2: We wanted to go far and we're out far too early. We'll need answers.
cup_L.firm_3: It's a big disappointment. Some players will have to show me something else.

hero.praise: He's becoming a truly great player.
hero.calm: He had a good game, like the whole team.
hero.firm: I'm happy for him, but he has to keep working.
hero.praise_2: He had a huge game. That lad's finishing is something special.
hero.praise_3: Tonight he carried the team. He deserves every compliment.
hero.calm_2: He was well served and he finished well. That's the work of the whole team.
hero.calm_3: I'm happy for him, but I won't single out one player after a team performance.
hero.firm_2: He scored, that's great. Now I want the same in the next game.
hero.firm_3: He knows what I expect. One good game isn't enough, he needs consistency.

streak_W.ambitious: We're confident and we don't plan to stop.
streak_W.humble: We don't look at the run, only at the next game.
streak_W.humour: I haven't changed my socks in a month. Back home, they're less thrilled than I am.
streak_W.ambitious_2: We've built momentum. Now we don't want to let go.
streak_W.ambitious_3: This team is hungry. And I'm not putting it on a diet.
streak_W.humble_2: It can end in the next game. We keep our feet on the ground.
streak_W.humble_3: We enjoy tonight, and from tomorrow we start from zero.
streak_W.humour_2: I'm not changing anything: same tie, same route, same coffee. Don't ask me to change.
streak_W.humour_3: I don't dare touch anything in the dressing room in case I break something.

streak_L.protect: The group is united. I won't give up on my players.
streak_L.selfCritical: I have to find solutions. That's my job and I'm not doing it well enough.
streak_L.firm: Enough is enough. Changes are needed, and there will be some.

streak_winless.protect: The group is working well. The win will come.
streak_winless.selfCritical: I'm still looking for the right formula. I take responsibility.
streak_winless.firm: We need to find our hunger again. Everyone is concerned, me first.
streak_winless.protect_2: The players aren't giving up. It will turn, I'm sure of it.
streak_winless.protect_3: I see the hunger in training. The breakthrough is coming.
streak_winless.selfCritical_2: I have to find the answer faster. That's my job.
streak_winless.selfCritical_3: Maybe I'm asking too much, or asking the wrong way. I'll rethink how I do things.
streak_winless.firm_2: It's time to wake up. Everyone, no exceptions.
streak_winless.firm_3: This is no longer acceptable. The next games will show who wants to fight.

streak_unbeaten.ambitious: We've become a very solid team, and we want to keep it going.
streak_unbeaten.humble: We're pleased, but the season is long.
streak_unbeaten.humour: Unbeatable? I'd rather not say it too loud, we play again in three days.
streak_unbeaten.ambitious_2: We're hard to beat and we want to stay that way all season.
streak_unbeaten.ambitious_3: That solidity is our strength. We want to go even further.
streak_unbeaten.humble_2: We don't lose, but we don't always win either. There's work to do.
streak_unbeaten.humble_3: A run earns you nothing on its own. Only points count.
streak_unbeaten.humour_2: Don't say the word. Runs always end when you talk about them.
streak_unbeaten.humour_3: I've been touching wood for so long I'll end up a carpenter.

youthDebut.praise: He has a rare talent. I'm proud he made his debut with us.
youthDebut.calm: A first game is a step. The hard part starts now.
youthDebut.firm: He earned his chance in training. He'll have to keep earning it.

bigWin.praise: We saw what this team is capable of. The players were huge.
bigWin.humble: A big score is still only three points. We keep our feet on the ground.
bigWin.humour: I asked the players to save a few for the next game.
bigWin.praise_2: Everything we've worked on for weeks, we saw tonight. Well done to the players.
bigWin.praise_3: This is the kind of game that does a whole club good.
bigWin.humble_2: We won't get carried away. The next game could be completely different.
bigWin.humble_3: They had a tough night. It can happen to us too, so we stay humble.
bigWin.humour_2: I think the players wanted to make me happy. Mission accomplished.
bigWin.humour_3: We may have used up all our goals for the month. I hope there are a few left.

runEnded.protect: I never doubted this group. They deserved this win.
runEnded.calm: It feels good, but it's only one win. We have to back it up.
runEnded.humour: We'd almost forgotten the taste. It comes back quickly.

pressure.confident: I have the backing of the chairman and the players. I'm calm.
pressure.selfCritical: The results aren't there, I know. It's up to me to change that.
pressure.firm: I don't comment on rumours. I work.

fans.confident: They're right to demand a lot. We'll put a smile back on their faces.
fans.selfCritical: I understand their anger. They deserve better than this.
fans.firm: I hear the boos. I just ask the fans to back the team for 90 minutes.

exClub.humble: I have a lot of respect for that club and its fans. But I'm here now.
exClub.deflect: It's a game like any other. What matters is my team.
exClub.tease: Revenge? Let's say I know the way to the away dressing room very well.

contract.confident: We're talking, and I'm confident. He's happy here.
contract.deflect: Contracts are discussed in offices, not in front of microphones.
contract.firm: Nobody is bigger than the club. If he wants to stay, the door is open.
contract.confident_2: He knows how much I value him. I think we'll reach an agreement.
contract.confident_3: Talks are going well. I'm not worried.
contract.deflect_2: That's between the player, his agent and the club. I'm thinking about the next game.
contract.deflect_3: I won't negotiate his contract in front of you. Ask me about the pitch.
contract.firm_2: The club has made an offer. Now the ball is in his court.
contract.firm_3: I want players who want to be here. We'll soon see if he's one of them.

unhappy.protect: I back him one hundred percent. He's going through a tough spell, we'll help him.
unhappy.deny: There's no problem at all. You should have seen him smiling in training this morning.
unhappy.firm: If he's not happy, my door is open. But the pitch decides.

signing.ambitious: He's a player who will take us up a level.
signing.calm: He needs to settle in first. We won't put pressure on him.
signing.praise: A top-quality player and an excellent person. We're delighted.
signing.ambitious_2: We signed him to take the next step. He has the qualities for it.
signing.ambitious_3: It's a strong signal for the dressing room and for our rivals.
signing.calm_2: He's discovering a new club and new team-mates. Let's give him time.
signing.calm_3: We'll bring him in gently. He has nothing to prove on day one.
signing.praise_2: I've wanted him for a long time. I'm happy he chose our project.
signing.praise_3: He has an exemplary mentality. He'll lift the whole group.

exit.praise: I thank him for everything he gave. I wish him all the best.
exit.deflect: It was the best decision for everyone. I won't say more.
exit.firm: Nobody is irreplaceable. We have what we need in the squad.

longInjury.confident: We have options. Someone else will take their chance.
longInjury.calm: It's hard for him. We'll support him all the way back.
longInjury.firm: No crying. The group has to make up for it.
longInjury.confident_2: It's a chance for others. I trust them.
longInjury.confident_3: We have depth. Someone will step up.
longInjury.calm_2: The most important thing is that he comes back healthy. We won't rush anything.
longInjury.calm_3: We think of him first. For the team, we'll find solutions.
longInjury.firm_2: Nobody will feel sorry for us. We have to move on without him.
longInjury.firm_3: It's hard, but it doesn't change our goals.

linked.deny: I'm one hundred percent focused on my club. There's nothing in it.
linked.deflect: I won't comment on rumours. The next game is all that matters.
linked.tease: My phone rings a lot. I don't always answer.

followUp_broken.confident: I stand by it. One defeat doesn't change what I think of this team.
followUp_broken.selfCritical: Maybe I spoke too soon. The facts proved me wrong tonight.
followUp_broken.humour: I see you take notes. I'll have to watch what I say.

followUp_kept.praise: The players answered on the pitch. That's all I asked for.
followUp_kept.humble: One win doesn't fix everything. We have to keep going like this.
followUp_kept.firm: The message was clear. I never want to see the last game again.

followUp_denied.deny: My answer hasn't changed. I'm here and I'm focused.
followUp_denied.humour: If I took every job I'm linked with, I'd be managing half of Europe.
followUp_denied.tease: I've never said never. But today, I'm here.

followUp_again.confident: Yes, and I believe it even more today.
followUp_again.selfCritical: Words are useless if we show nothing on the pitch. It's up to us to prove it.
followUp_again.humour: You have a good memory. I hope the players do too.

ingame.thanks: Answers sent to FM Immersion. Thanks, boss!
ingame.inGame: You can also answer right inside FM27: the press window opens over the game (F8 key).

coachLife.title: Off the pitch
coachLife.intro: Your coach's life away from the club: what your career has earned you, your family and the big moments. Everything stays in the app, nothing is changed in your save.

money.title: Personal finances
money.help: Enter the salary for each club (you'll find it in your contract, on your manager profile in FM27). The app counts the days spent at each club.
money.missing_one: One club has no salary yet: it isn't counted in the totals.
money.missing_other: {{count}} clubs have no salary yet: they aren't counted in the totals.
money.choices: Including housing {{housing}}, car {{car}}, phone choices {{oneOff}}, badges {{badges}}.

home.title: Family
home.help: Your family, if you want to give it a place in your career. Children's ages follow the game date.

phone.title: Phone
phone.empty: No new messages. More will come with the big moments of your career: joining a club, a title, the end of a season, leaving.
phone.note: Your answers stay in the app: they change your finances, your family and your gauges, not your FM27 save.

gauges.title: Your personal life
gauges.note_zero: Answer the phone messages to move the gauges.

harmonyMood.low: Things are a bit tense at home: think of them.
harmonyMood.crisis: Your family is in crisis: time to slow down.

moraleMood.high: You're at the top of your game.

badges.title: Coaching badges
badges.help: Paid out of your own pocket, one at a time, even without a club. The cost comes out of your savings.
badges.note: In FM27, remember to start the course from your manager profile: the app doesn't put it in the game.

arrival.text: Welcome to {{club}}! I have a few places to show you. What do you fancy?

move.text: So it's {{club}}… Are we moving again? We need to talk.

car.text: New job, new car? I've got just what you need for the drive to {{club}}.

sacked.text: I saw the news about {{club}}. Are you OK? What are you going to do now?

choice.work: Get back to work right away

left.text: The {{club}} staff want to throw you a leaving do. Shall we?

trophy.text: {{trophy}} with {{club}}! The dressing room is on fire. How do you celebrate?

done.family: Family weekend to celebrate the title

birth.text: {{name}} is born! Can you take a few days off?

done.leave: A few days at home for {{name}}'s birth
done.stay: Stayed at the club when {{name}} was born

summer.text: The {{season}} season is over! Where are we going this summer?
